name: Inuko bond prices LP from the pair's raw USDT balance
summary: The Inuko bond contract valued LP as 2 x USDT.balanceOf(pair) x lpAmount / totalSupply and quoted that in INUKO via getAmountsIn. The attacker flash-borrowed USDT, sent it to the INUKO/USDT pair, bought bonds with LP while the balance was inflated, skimmed the USDT back, and claimed the oversized INUKO payouts after the lock expired.
notes: The reset is owner addBond() listing the INUKO/USDT pair as bond 0's lpToken, whose raw USDT balance LpToToken reads; later deposits and activation only funded the bond.

Campaign: two copycat EOAs replayed the attack with the same contract bytecode in three more buyBond transactions; the four claim transactions that paid the manipulated bonds out are listed because the bond's INUKO left only there.
INUKO has no price; it is valued at what the exploiters realised, the USDT their EOAs received from selling the claimed INUKO into the pair. The LP they paid is not netted (rule 14).
